metadata.title: Deterministic vs. Probabilistic AI
metadata.audience: Anyone who builds with AI or relies on its output

beats.narration_text: Ask an AI the same question twice and you can get two different answers. For brainstorming, that's fine. For your company's financials, it's a problem. The real question isn't whether AI is smart. It's when probably right is good enough, and when you need provably right.

props.command: Same question, two different answers. When is that okay?
output: Probably right: great for ideas and drafts.
Provably right: required for money, identity, safety.
Pick the tool by what the job can tolerate.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Asavari, a fellow at Humanitarians AI. This video is about the difference between deterministic and probabilistic systems, AI that gives its best guess, versus code that gives the exact same answer every single time. You'll learn when guessing is fine, when it's dangerous, and how to tell which one a job actually needs. If you build with AI or depend on its output, this is for you.

props.command: What is this video about, and why should I watch it?
output: Who: Asavari, a Humanitarians AI fellow
What: deterministic vs. probabilistic — guess vs. proof
Why watch: know when a guess is too risky to ship

beats.narration_text: A probabilistic system samples. Same input, and the output can shift, a different word, a different number, a different conclusion. It can be brilliant and confident, and still not repeatable. And if you can't reproduce an answer, you can't audit it. For anything that has to be checked, defended, or trusted, a confident guess is not enough.

artifactLines: Probabilistic = samples; the output can shift run to run
Confident and fluent is not the same as repeatable
Can't reproduce it -> can't audit it
props.sparkLine: A confident guess is not proof.

beats.narration_text: A deterministic system does the opposite. Same input, same output, every time, with a trail you can follow from result back to source. Rules and lookups instead of sampling. The move is to split the work: put the parts that must be exact, the math, the identifiers, the money, into deterministic code, and let the AI handle the fuzzy, forgiving parts, like phrasing or drafting. Right tool, right job.

props.artifactTitle: Same input, same output — with a trail
props.artifactHeading: split the work by what must be exact
artifactLines: Deterministic = rules + lookups; identical result every time
Exact parts (math, IDs, money) -> deterministic code
Fuzzy parts (phrasing, drafting) -> let the AI help

beats.narration_text: But you can't make everything deterministic. Language, judgment, and ambiguity genuinely need a probabilistic model, that's its strength. The skill is drawing the line: which steps must be exact, money, identity, safety, and which can tolerate a good guess. Put a guess where you needed a receipt, and it will pass every demo, right up until it costs you.

props.artifactTitle: Draw the line by the stakes
props.artifactHeading: not everything can — or should — be deterministic
artifactLines: Language, judgment, ambiguity -> a probabilistic model shines
Money, identity, safety -> must be exact
A guess where you needed a receipt passes every demo — until it doesn't
props.sparkLine: Don't put a guess where you need proof.

beats.narration_text: Before you trust AI in a workflow, ask four things. Does this step need the same answer every time? Can I trace how it got there? What's the cost if it's wrong? And should the AI even be in the critical path? Match the tool to the stakes. Use the guess where a guess is safe, and keep it out where you need proof.

props.artifactTitle: Match the tool to the stakes
props.artifactHeading: Use the guess where it's safe; keep it out where you need proof
artifactLines: Does this step need the same answer every time?
Can I trace how it got there?
What does a wrong answer cost?
Should the AI be in the critical path at all?
